summary: Wheeler County lookout first built of logs in 1935, cabin added 1936; abandoned, with the tower reported collapsed in a June 2021 windstorm.

facts.design: wooden lookout tower: 60 ft in 1935-36 descriptions; 50 ft with a 14x14 cab in the 1951 annual report and firelookout.com's 1952 entry
facts.status_note: Listed by firelookout.com as abandoned; the tower is reported collapsed in a June 2021 windstorm (single source)

staffing.status: lookout R.P. Parrish named in 1939; fire reports kept through the 1964 season

facts.agency: Forest Service (Umatilla National Forest) in 1936; Oregon Department of Forestry by 1952, per firelookout.com

events.note: tower of logs and lumber built for $300; firelookout.com records a 60-foot wooden tower
Forest Service was building a 10x10 foot cabin on the tower (July 30, 1936 newspaper: 'is building')
lookout R.P. Parrish laid off with the flu; Owen Leathers to relieve him

50-foot tower with 14x14 cabin recorded in the Central Oregon District annual report; firelookout.com dates the 50-foot ODF tower to 1952. The sources do not say when or why the height changed from 60 ft.
seven-mile telephone line from Kinzua added for telephone and remote radio
someone climbed to the catwalk and shot through the building shutters
station included as a radio relay point for the change over to FM; nine fire discoveries that season
FM antenna installed on a 90-foot round timber pole
tower collapsed during a June 2021 windstorm, per firelookout.com only

corrections.why: 3.0 m appears in neither source; the 1951 annual report gives a 50-foot tower (15.2 m), and firelookout.com gives 50 ft for 1952 and 60 ft for 1935

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1936 Forest Service description places the lookout about six miles southeast of Kinzua; firelookout.com places it six miles northwest of Winlock. Both are quoted in the story; neither is adopted over the other.
Sources give 60 ft (1935-36) and 50 ft (1951 annual report; firelookout.com 1952). height_m uses the 50-foot figure, which both sources date to the 1950s; no source explains the change in height.
The 1936 cabin was a Forest Service project; firelookout.com lists the tower as Oregon Department of Forestry. Both are kept in the agency fact.

notes_for_editor: The 2021 collapse rests on firelookout.com alone (no second source found in a web search); the story says so. Height_m uses the 50-foot 1951 tower and is proposed as a correction to 3.0 m. Location conflicts (Kinzua vs Winlock) are unresolved; the record coordinate (44.96047, -119.98998) was not checked against either description. Access level 'closed' follows firelookout.com's 'No public access.' with no reason given.
